# Verified wallet Pro grants

Base: 99077c0b804b5cd906221546907be15fa1e604c4. Risk R2 authorization/entitlement. Next16.3.4 React19.2.6 ethers5.8.0. Existing holder access uses email-authenticated revocable sessions, nonce-bound ownership signatures, confirmed Robinhood EOA/token checks and database proof context. WalletConnect authority R3 slice already committed; no cryptographic/proof behavior changes here.

## Scope and ownership
User explicitly grants Pro to one wallet; root records that exact authorized target in private deployment evidence. Root configures a server-only Vercel PRO_WALLET_ALLOWLIST setting and owns integration/deploy. Sol High complex builder owns src/server/public-wallet-grants.ts (new), public-holder.ts, public-services.ts, src/lib/pro-access.ts, src/components/ProAccess.tsx, relevant tests, .env.example and narrow HOSTING.md documentation. One writer in isolated ../wallet-pro-grant; theme worker separately owns only presentation CSS/hero. No worker subagents, dependencies, migrations or provider writes.

## Contract/invariants
- PRO_WALLET_ALLOWLIST is an optional bounded comma-separated list of exact nonzero40hex EVM addresses. Normalize case after syntactic validation. No wildcard/prefix/substring matching, client input or NEXT_PUBLIC override. Missing/empty/malformed/oversized config grants nobody; normal subscriptions/holder access remain independent. Use at most100 entries and bounded input.
- Do NOT hardcode owner's address into public source/default/example. Root supplies actual address only in server hosting config. Show only the authenticated user's linked address already returned by existing holder API, never the full list.
- Add HolderAccess.granted boolean, false in default/failed/unverified results. Only set it after existing holderAccess has passed valid current-session proof, confirmed EOA/token/chain balance read and fresh proof-context reread. Do not change verifyHolder, nonce/message generation, signature checks, context or DB procedures. Grant bypasses token quantity and payment requirement only; does not bypass ownership, session, quota, chain/RPC availability or other server protections.
- getProStatus and requirePro treat verified holder.granted as another positive entitlement alongside subscription or holder.eligible. Keep token holder.eligible tied strictly to the666666 RICH threshold; never fabricate a balance/subscription. Existing deadlines and independent provider failure behavior persist.
- Client displays Pro active / wallet grant explicitly and does not label grant as subscription or qualifying token holdings. Grant users can still manage existing subscriptions; no automatic cancellation or charges. Avoid unnecessary subscription upsell for granted-only users. Tell granted wallet users to use existing email sign-in + Verify holding wallet proof flow. Unlink/logout/session expiry or configuration removal must end grant through existing refresh/enforcement paths.
- Preserve US$15 subscription,666666 threshold, WalletConnect shared provider identity/version, all signatures/financial handlers, LIVE_LAUNCH_ENABLED=false and protection. No secret/owner .env.local exposure.

## Verification and operating gap
Focused tests: absent/invalid/oversized config, exact/case-normalized match, nearby/nonmember/zero addresses denied; unverified/expired/mismatched/revoked proof denied even if allowlisted; zero token balance with valid allowlisted proof grants; nonmember holder threshold and paid subscription remain unchanged; RPC/proof failure fails closed; env removal revokes; server requirePro shares decision; UI distinguishes grant. Run relevant existing tests in isolated worktree using existing dependencies; no installs or builds against root artifacts. Root owns final combined full suite/typecheck/build/scans/audit, independent Sol verification and fresh Astra review before protected deployment.

A new dedicated business Supabase project (`wslrotrrcrytbvxidqnm`, Sydney) is healthy, and reviewed migrations001/002 have been applied to its previously empty public schema. Its URL/anon/service-role settings and the authorized server-only wallet allowlist are configured in Vercel Production; values were not exposed. A sensitive Stripe key is also configured, but its account/mode have not been independently verified and the webhook secret is absent. Migration003 remains unapplied pending exact-candidate independent verification and review. Supabase's free default email provider rejected the code-template change without custom SMTP or an upgrade, so public email-code sign-in and real grant proof remain blocked. Production subscription synchronization is also unverified. No live fund actions or signing enablement.

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Address string spoofing | Medium | Existing signed current-session proof required before exact config match |
| Grant misreported as token holding/subscription | Medium | Separate granted flag and explicit UI status |
| Revocation ignored in client cache | Medium | Server rechecks every privileged call, existing focus/minute refresh |
| Missing account services | Present | Report configured/pending, fail closed; no browser-only bypass |

Key principle: waive the price and balance threshold for the verified owner, never the ownership check.

## Added user request: subscription records in Supabase
User explicitly asks to wire subscriptions into the Supabase store. This adds R2 billing/schema scope to this same server slice. Builder also owns db/003_subscription_store.sql, src/server/public-subscription-store.ts, pages/api/stripe-webhook.ts and focused tests. No change to current authoritative Stripe access checks or checkout intent semantics.

Design: persist HOODLABS subscription snapshots (subscription/customer/price IDs, status, period end, cancel-at-period-end and canceled/ended dates as applicable) plus a minimal event receipt ledger. Resolve ownership ONLY via existing unique hood_billing.customer_id; never bind another user using webhook metadata/client_reference_id. Ignore unrelated customers/products and unknown event types. Support customer.subscription.created/updated/deleted and subscription Checkout completion; validate live/test mode matches actual Stripe client/event. A signed event is a synchronization trigger, not an entitlement grant. Retrieve the current subscription from Stripe, confirm customer and configured price, then persist only an allowlisted data projection (no raw payment/customer payload).

Replay/concurrency: use transactional service-only RPCs to begin/complete synchronization. Each begin obtains a monotonically increasing per-subscription version in PostgreSQL; already completed event IDs are acknowledged idempotently, pending/failed retries may obtain a new version. Complete commits only if the version is still current and customer/user binding unchanged, then marks that event processed atomically. A superseded response must not overwrite a newer snapshot or mark success; return a retriable failure. Even delayed old events fetch CURRENT Stripe data. Mark no event processed before successful snapshot commit. Store failures return5xx to let Stripe retry. Bounds/checks on IDs/status/date fields, RLS and revocation for anon/authenticated; service_role only. No new dependency or cache-based Pro grants.

Test signature/raw-body enforcement and replay, duplicate concurrent begin/complete, stale completion rejection, outage/retry, delayed events/current retrieval, wrong customer/account/price/mode rejection, deletion/cancellation and real SQL privileges using existing PGlite pattern. Required full combined review before applying new migration. Root may prepare a NEW isolated business Supabase project and apply existing reviewed001/002;003 waits for exact-candidate independent verification/review. No changes to unrelated existing projects. Runtime Stripe secret may still require user provision; do not route public app calls through the owner's Composio token or claim production synchronization without real webhook verification. Live signing/Checkout remain disabled.
